title: service-job: `db-job-adapter.timeout.test.ts` reds CI whenever the run crosses a minute boundary — it registers a real every-minute cron and asserts exactly one run row
body:
Found while verifying an unrelated change (#8460 / PR #8620), where this test reddened `Test Core (2/3)` on a diff that cannot reach it. Filing rather than fixing — out of scope for that card.

## The failure

```
FAIL  src/db-job-adapter.timeout.test.ts
  > the timeout policy still applies through an injected cron adapter (#7734)
  > a cron-scheduled run lands a timeout row even though the adapter no longer sees the policy

AssertionError: expected [ { …(10) }, { …(7) } ] to have a length of 1 but got 2
 ❯ src/db-job-adapter.timeout.test.ts:221:18
```

## Why it flakes

The case registers a **real** `CronJobAdapter` (croner) on an every-minute expression, then fires one explicit trigger and asserts exactly one persisted run row:

```ts
const CRON = { type: 'cron', expression: '* * * * *' } as const;  // line 48
...
const cron = new CronJobAdapter();
const adapter = new DbJobAdapter({ engine, cron });
await adapter.schedule('cronic', CRON, handler, { timeout: TIMEOUT_MS });
await cron.trigger('cronic');            // the explicit fire the case is about

const runs = engine.tables.get('sys_job_run') ?? [];
expect(runs).toHaveLength(1);            // line 221 — fails as 2
```

Nothing suppresses the cron's **own** schedule. If the wall clock crosses a minute boundary between `adapter.schedule(...)` and the assertion, croner fires the registration independently and a second `sys_job_run` row lands — so the count is 2, not 1.

The failing CI run makes the mechanism explicit rather than inferred:

- test file `Start at 03:02:55`
- assertion failure stamped `03:03:00.17`

i.e. the run straddled `03:03:00`, which is exactly when `* * * * *` fires.

## Evidence it is timing, not a real regression

- Passes locally 5/5 in isolation, and the whole package passes (8 files / 71 tests) on the same commit that reds it in CI.
- `@objectstack/service-job` does **not** depend on `@objectstack/objectql` (`dependencies`: `core`, `metadata-core`, `platform-objects`, `spec`), so the change it reddened has no dependency path to it at all.
- The case never touches the object fold, labels, or metadata reads — it drives a fake in-memory engine.

## Why it matters

It is a **wall-clock-positional** flake, not a random one: any CI run whose service-job shard happens to straddle a minute boundary reds, and the red points at a package the offending PR often has not touched. That is expensive to diagnose — it cost one dev-agent cycle here, and the shard attestation surfaces it a second time as an aggregate `Test Core` red, which reads like two failures.

## Suggested direction (not prescriptive)

Make the case's cron unable to self-fire, so the explicit trigger is the only writer — e.g. a far-future/never expression, faking timers around the registration, or registering through a cron double whose schedule is inert while `trigger()` still works. The case's stated intent (#7734: the timeout policy survives the policy-free registration handed to the timer adapter) does not depend on the cron actually being schedulable.

⚠️ Any in-memory `matches(row, where)` double introduced here must satisfy `pnpm check:where-matcher` or throw.

## Repro

```
pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-job test
```
straddling a minute boundary — or set the clock so `adapter.schedule` lands within a few hundred ms of `:00`.
